column1: # catalog/ci-batch-escalate.tsv — which changed paths make a Mergify merge-queue
# batch run the WHOLE corpus instead of its impact set (BH-4968). Read by
# bin/lib/ci-batch-escalate.sh, which bin/ci-plan.sh asks once per changed path
#   pattern  ending in / : a prefix (bin/lib/ matches everything under bin/lib)
#            anything else: a bash glob matched against the whole path
#   kind     escalate | allow. An allow row exempts a path an escalate row
#            would catch. Rows of any other kind belong to another reader and
#   why      one line, for the reviewer of this file
# KINDS spa AND worker (BH-4969) are read by cbe_affects, not cbe_reason (which
# skips them). On a batch that stays batch-selected, bin/ci-plan.sh writes
# spa=0 (worker=0) when no changed path is affected, and the console-ui
# (worker-jobs) job then runs only its "not affected by this batch" step. A
# path under console-ui/ (worker/) is always affected, row or no row; these rows
# add the paths OUTSIDE those trees each job builds or tests from: what
# console-ui/ and worker/jobs/ import or read by a relative path (a guard in
# tests/ci-plan-spa-worker.bh-4969-test.sh fails on one with no row here), and
# the scripts the jobs' own workflow steps run. A path that also escalates still
# carries its row, so deleting an escalate row cannot un-gate a job. Every
# non-batch-selected run, and an escalated batch, runs both jobs whole.
# These are the paths the selection itself runs on: the workflow, the planner,
# the selector and tier step, the libs and catalogs those three source and read,
# the runners, and the suites' shared helpers. A batch that touches one of them
# cannot trust a selection that the change may have altered, so it proves
# everything. The file fails closed: unreadable, or no escalate row, escalates
# BH-6059 replaced the blanket `bin/lib/` and `catalog/` rows with the files
# below: 19 of 21 sampled batches ran the whole corpus through them, a README
# included. Every other bin/lib/ or catalog/ path runs its impact set, and one
# the impact map has no specific row for (a new file, a deleted one) still

# escalates, as `unmapped path

`: bin/test-impact.sh does that under
# TI_BATCH_SELECT=1, which only bin/ci-plan.sh's batch select sets. The rows
# are derived from what the scripts source and read; a guard in
# test-impact's infra list has no row here. Not rows, on purpose:
# catalog/ci-suite-durations.tsv (shard weights, not which suites run),
# never read when a batch is selected).
# The allow rows exempt docs: a *.md never escalates on its own.
